title: Finite-presentation ring chart and its base-change flatness predicates
statement: For a preorder $J$ with chosen element $j_0$, a ring chart consists of a functor $F:J\to\mathrm{CommRing}$, two commutative rings $B,C$ with $F(j_0)$-algebra structures, an algebra homomorphism $\phi:B\to C$, and a proof that $\phi$ is finitely presented. For a homomorphism $q:F(j_0)\to R$, its base-flat predicate is flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of $\mathrm{id}_R\otimes\phi:R\otimes_{F(j_0)} B\to R\otimes_{F(j_0)} C$. Its stage-flat predicate at $j_0\le j$ uses $q=F(j_0\le j)$; its limit-flat predicate uses the coprojection to the categorical colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This is a structure of ring data and its properties, without selecting any chart or witness.
